---
title: "04 - MOFA Model Fitting"
subtitle: "Corrected Prov-GigaPath embeddings integrated with molecular views"
format: html
editor: visual
---

Fits one MOFA+ model per cancer type, integrating the corrected slide embedding
with RNA-seq, RPPA, copy number and miRNA. A second model per cancer uses the
raw embeddings; it is used only in 05 to check that batch correction carries
through to the latent factors.

Inputs: `embed_corrected_by_cancer.rds`, `embed_raw_by_cancer.rds`,
`meta_corrected_by_cancer.rds`, `omics_by_cancer.rds`

Outputs: `mofa/mofa_<CANCER>_<corrected|raw>.hdf5`, `mofa_input_summary.rds`

## Libraries

```{r, message=FALSE}
#| output: false
library(MOFA2)
library(dplyr)
library(gt)
library(ggplot2)
```

## Load data

```{r load}
data_dir <- "data"
mofa_dir <- "mofa"
dir.create(mofa_dir, showWarnings = FALSE)

embed_corrected_by_cancer <- readRDS(file.path(data_dir, "embed_corrected_by_cancer.rds"))
embed_raw_by_cancer       <- readRDS(file.path(data_dir, "embed_raw_by_cancer.rds"))
meta_corrected_by_cancer  <- readRDS(file.path(data_dir, "meta_corrected_by_cancer.rds"))
omics_by_cancer           <- readRDS(file.path(data_dir, "omics_by_cancer.rds"))

main_cancers <- c("KIRC", "COAD", "LUAD", "OV", "READ")
mofa_cancers <- intersect(main_cancers, names(embed_corrected_by_cancer))
cat("Cancers:", paste(mofa_cancers, collapse = ", "), "\n")
```

## Config

```{r config}
# Molecular views: short view name -> curatedTCGAData experiment pattern
view_patterns <- c(RNA   = "RNASeq2GeneNorm",
                   RPPA  = "RPPAArray",
                   CNV   = "GISTIC_AllByGene",
                   miRNA = "miRNASeqGene")

# Features kept per view, by variance (NULL keeps all). Full 20k-gene matrices
# dominate the model and slow convergence.
n_top <- list(RNA = 5000, RPPA = NULL, CNV = 5000, miRNA = 500)

min_samples_view <- 20      # drop a view observed in fewer patients
n_factors        <- 15
convergence      <- "slow"  # "fast" for testing only
versions_to_fit  <- c("corrected", "raw")
overwrite        <- TRUE    # TRUE refits every model; set FALSE to skip models already on disk
set.seed(42)
```

## Remove old models

Models fitted with earlier versions of this file are deleted, so every model is
refitted with the current view preparation. Skipped when `overwrite` is FALSE.

```{r clean}
if (overwrite) {
  old <- list.files(mofa_dir, pattern = "\\.hdf5$", full.names = TRUE)
  if (length(old) > 0) { file.remove(old); cat("Removed", length(old), "old model files\n") }
}
```

## Available views

```{r views}
view_avail <- sapply(mofa_cancers, function(cc) {
  sapply(view_patterns, function(p) any(grepl(p, names(omics_by_cancer[[cc]]))))
})
print(view_avail)   # all TRUE expected
```

## Helper functions

```{r helpers}
# One assay as a numeric matrix with unique feature names.
# Experiments are named like "OV_RNASeq2GeneNorm-20160128"; match by pattern.
get_assay <- function(omics_list, pattern) {
  idx <- grep(pattern, names(omics_list), ignore.case = TRUE)
  if (length(idx) == 0) return(NULL)
  x <- omics_list[[idx[1]]]

  if (methods::is(x, "SummarizedExperiment")) {
    m  <- SummarizedExperiment::assay(x)
    rd <- SummarizedExperiment::rowData(x)
    if (is.null(rownames(m)) && "Gene.Symbol" %in% names(rd))
      rownames(m) <- rd$Gene.Symbol
  } else {
    m <- as.matrix(x)
  }

  if (is.null(rownames(m)))
    stop(pattern, " has no feature names; set rownames when building omics_by_cancer")
  rownames(m) <- make.unique(as.character(rownames(m)))
  storage.mode(m) <- "numeric"
  m
}

# Transform, filter, and keep the top-variance features of one view
prep_view <- function(mat, view, top_n = NULL) {
  # Keep only patients who have this assay. Missingness below is then judged
  # among measured patients, so a view measured in fewer than half the cohort
  # (e.g. miRNA in KIRC) is not dropped entirely. Missing patients are
  # re-added as NA by align_samples().
  mat <- mat[, colSums(!is.na(mat)) > 0, drop = FALSE]

  # Count-scale views are log-transformed, unless already on a log scale (negatives present)
  if (view %in% c("RNA", "miRNA") && min(mat, na.rm = TRUE) >= 0) {
    if (view == "miRNA")                                     # raw read counts: correct for sequencing depth
      mat <- sweep(mat, 2, colSums(mat, na.rm = TRUE), "/") * 1e6   # counts per million
    mat <- log2(mat + 1)
  }

  mat  <- mat[rowMeans(is.na(mat)) < 0.5, , drop = FALSE]   # features missing in most measured patients
  v    <- apply(mat, 1, var, na.rm = TRUE)
  keep <- which(v > 0)                                       # drops NA and constant features
  keep <- keep[order(v[keep], decreasing = TRUE)]            # most variable first
  if (!is.null(top_n)) keep <- head(keep, top_n)
  mat[keep, , drop = FALSE]
}

# MOFA requires identical samples (columns) in every view; missing = NA
align_samples <- function(mat, samples) {
  out <- matrix(NA_real_, nrow(mat), length(samples),
                dimnames = list(rownames(mat), samples))
  common <- intersect(colnames(mat), samples)
  out[, common] <- mat[, common]
  out
}

# Build the view list for one cancer. Both versions use the same patients.
build_views <- function(cc, embed_source) {
  samples <- rownames(embed_corrected_by_cancer[[cc]])       # corrected patients define the cohort
  stopifnot(all(samples %in% rownames(embed_source[[cc]])))

  emb <- t(as.matrix(embed_source[[cc]][samples, , drop = FALSE]))   # features x patients
  if (is.null(rownames(emb))) rownames(emb) <- paste0("emb_", seq_len(nrow(emb)))
  views <- list(Embedding = emb)

  for (v in names(view_patterns)) {
    m <- get_assay(omics_by_cancer[[cc]], view_patterns[[v]])
    if (is.null(m)) next

    m     <- align_samples(prep_view(m, v, n_top[[v]]), samples)    # NA where a patient lacks the assay
    n_obs <- sum(colSums(!is.na(m)) > 0)
    if (nrow(m) < 2 || n_obs < min_samples_view) {
      cat("  ", v, ": ", nrow(m), " features, ", n_obs, " patients, dropped\n", sep = "")
      next
    }

    # Unique feature names across views: suffixes keep RNA gene symbols untouched,
    # so the GSEA in 05 can match RNA weights to Hallmark gene sets
    if (v %in% c("RPPA", "CNV")) rownames(m) <- paste0(rownames(m), "_", tolower(v))
    views[[v]] <- m
    cat("  ", v, ": ", nrow(m), " features x ", n_obs, " patients\n", sep = "")
  }
  views
}

# Slim metadata stored in the model; full metadata is joined in 05
build_meta <- function(cc, samples) {
  m <- meta_corrected_by_cancer[[cc]][samples, , drop = FALSE]
  data.frame(sample   = samples,
             Cancer   = cc,
             TSS.Code = as.character(m$TSS.Code),
             time     = as.numeric(as.character(m$time)),   # safe if stored as factor
             event    = as.numeric(as.character(m$event)),
             stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
}

fit_mofa <- function(views, meta_slim, outfile) {
  obj <- create_mofa(views)
  samples_metadata(obj) <- meta_slim

  data_opts <- get_default_data_options(obj)
  data_opts$scale_views <- TRUE     # views are on very different scales

  model_opts <- get_default_model_options(obj)
  model_opts$num_factors <- n_factors

  train_opts <- get_default_training_options(obj)
  train_opts$convergence_mode <- convergence
  train_opts$seed <- 42

  obj <- prepare_mofa(obj, data_options = data_opts,
                      model_options = model_opts, training_options = train_opts)
  run_mofa(obj, outfile = outfile, use_basilisk = TRUE)
}
```



## Figure S4.1 and Table S4.1 Dimensionality of each view

**Purpose:** shows how concentrated each view's variation is. **How to read:**
a view whose cumulative curve rises steeply (e.g. CNV, where neighbouring genes
share copy-number segments) is dominated by a few directions that a 15-factor
model captures easily. A flat curve (e.g. the embedding) means variation is
spread over many directions. The value at 15 PCs is the most variance any
15-component linear model could explain in that view alone, so it is an upper
bound on that view's total in Figure 5.1B. PCA uses the matrices MOFA receives,
centred per feature as MOFA does.

```{r view_dimensionality, fig.width=12, fig.height=6}
view_cols <- c(Embedding = "#1b9e77", RNA = "#d95f02", RPPA = "#7570b3",
               CNV = "#e7298a", miRNA = "#66a61e")             # same palette as 05

# PCA of one prepared view (features x patients), on the patients who have that view
pca_view <- function(m) {
  m <- m[, colSums(!is.na(m)) > 0, drop = FALSE]               # patients measured in this view
  if (anyNA(m)) {                                              # scattered gaps: feature mean
    mu  <- rowMeans(m, na.rm = TRUE)
    idx <- which(is.na(m), arr.ind = TRUE)
    m[idx] <- mu[idx[, "row"]]
  }
  X  <- t(m)                                                   # patients x features
  ev <- prcomp(X, center = TRUE, scale. = FALSE)$sdev^2        # variance of each PC
  # Check: the PCs together hold all of the view's variance
  stopifnot(isTRUE(all.equal(sum(ev), sum(apply(X, 2, var)))))
  data.frame(PC = seq_along(ev),
             Var = 100 * ev / sum(ev),                         # % of view variance per PC
             Cum = 100 * cumsum(ev) / sum(ev),                 # cumulative %
             Patients = nrow(X), Features = ncol(X))
}

dim_df <- bind_rows(lapply(mofa_cancers, function(cc) {
  invisible(capture.output(views <- build_views(cc, embed_corrected_by_cancer)))  # same input as MOFA
  bind_rows(lapply(names(views), function(v) pca_view(views[[v]]) %>% mutate(Cancer = cc, View = v)))
})) %>%
  mutate(View   = factor(View, levels = names(view_cols)),
         Cancer = factor(Cancer, levels = mofa_cancers))

# Table S4.1: one row per cancer and view
dim_tab <- dim_df %>%
  group_by(Cancer, View) %>%
  summarise(Patients = first(Patients), Features = first(Features),
            PC1      = Var[1],                                 # share of the single largest direction
            Top15    = Cum[min(15, n())],                      # upper bound for 15 factors
            PCs_80   = which(Cum >= 80)[1],                    # PCs needed for 80% of variance
            Eff_dim  = sum(Var)^2 / sum(Var^2),                # effective number of dimensions
            .groups  = "drop")

dim_tab %>%
  gt(groupname_col = "Cancer") %>%
  fmt_number(columns = c(PC1, Top15, Eff_dim), decimals = 1) %>%
  cols_label(PC1 = "PC1 (%)", Top15 = "First 15 PCs (%)",
             PCs_80 = "PCs for 80%", Eff_dim = "Effective dimensions") %>%
  tab_header(title = "Table S4.1 Dimensionality of each MOFA input view",
             subtitle = "PCA of the prepared views; first 15 PCs = upper bound for a 15-factor model") %>%
  tab_footnote("Effective dimensions = (sum of eigenvalues)\u00b2 / sum of squared eigenvalues; 1 = one direction holds all variance.") %>%
  tab_options(table.font.size = 11, heading.align = "center")

# Figure S4.1: scree (top) and cumulative variance (bottom), first 50 PCs
plot_df <- bind_rows(
  dim_df %>% transmute(Cancer, View, PC, value = Var, Measure = "Variance per PC (%)"),
  dim_df %>% transmute(Cancer, View, PC, value = Cum, Measure = "Cumulative variance (%)")) %>%
  filter(PC <= 50) %>%
  mutate(Measure = factor(Measure, levels = c("Variance per PC (%)", "Cumulative variance (%)")))

figS4_1 <- ggplot(plot_df, aes(PC, value, colour = View)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 15, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey60") +   # number of MOFA factors
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.7) +
  facet_grid(Measure ~ Cancer, scales = "free_y", switch = "y") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = view_cols) +
  labs(title = "Figure S4.1 Dimensionality of MOFA input views",
       subtitle = "PCA of each prepared view; dashed line = 15 MOFA factors",
       x = "Principal component", y = NULL, colour = NULL) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 10) +
  theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank(), strip.placement = "outside",
        strip.background = element_rect(fill = "grey95", colour = NA),
        strip.text = element_text(face = "bold"), legend.position = "bottom")

figS4_1
ggsave(file.path("figures", "FigS4_1_view_dimensionality.pdf"), figS4_1, width = 12, height = 6)
```



* Copy-number variation was concentrated in few directions (85–90% of its variance in the first 15 principal components in COAD, KIRC and READ; Table S4.1), consistent with large correlated genomic segments, and dominated the leading MOFA factors. Dimensionality alone did not explain the embedding’s small contribution: RNA was more dispersed than the embedding (about 45% versus 50–65% in 15 components), yet MOFA explained substantially more RNA variance. The embedding’s low variance explained therefore reflects limited sharing with the molecular views; most morphological variation encoded by Prov-GigaPath is not captured by bulk molecular profiles, consistent with its independent prognostic value (Table 3.3).


## Fit models

Two models per cancer (corrected and raw embedding), 10 in total. Each view line
should show features x patients; every cancer should keep all five views.

```{r fit}
for (cc in mofa_cancers) {
  for (ver in versions_to_fit) {

    outfile <- file.path(normalizePath(mofa_dir), paste0("mofa_", cc, "_", ver, ".hdf5"))
    if (file.exists(outfile) && !overwrite) {
      cat(cc, ver, ": exists, skipping\n"); next
    }

    cat("\n==== Fitting", cc, "(", ver, ") ====\n")
    src   <- if (ver == "corrected") embed_corrected_by_cancer else embed_raw_by_cancer
    views <- build_views(cc, src)

    if (length(views) < 2) {
      cat("  fewer than 2 views, skipping\n"); next
    }

    tryCatch(
      fit_mofa(views, build_meta(cc, colnames(views$Embedding)), outfile),
      error = function(e) cat("  MOFA failed:", conditionMessage(e), "\n")
    )
  }
}
```

## Table 4.1 MOFA models

**Purpose:** documents what entered each model: patients, features per view and
number of factors. **How to read:** both versions of a cancer should have the
same patients and molecular views; only the embedding differs. Total variance
explained per view is shown graphically in Figure 5.1B.

```{r summary}
mofa_files <- list.files(mofa_dir, pattern = "^mofa_.*\\.hdf5$", full.names = TRUE)

mofa_summary <- bind_rows(lapply(mofa_files, function(f) {
  parts <- strsplit(sub("\\.hdf5$", "", basename(f)), "_")[[1]]
  m     <- suppressWarnings(load_model(f))
  dims  <- get_dimensions(m)
  r2    <- get_variance_explained(m)$r2_total[[1]]

  data.frame(Cancer = parts[2], Version = parts[3],
             Samples = sum(dims$N), Factors = dims$K,
             Views = paste(names(dims$D), dims$D, sep = "=", collapse = ", "),
             as.list(setNames(round(r2, 1), paste0("R2_", names(r2)))),
             check.names = FALSE)
})) %>% arrange(Cancer, Version)

mofa_summary %>%
  gt() %>%
  tab_header(title = "Table 4.1 MOFA models",
             subtitle = "Features per view and total variance explained (%) per view") %>%
  sub_missing(missing_text = "-") %>%
  tab_options(table.font.size = 11, heading.align = "center")

saveRDS(mofa_summary, file.path(data_dir, "mofa_input_summary.rds"))
```

## Data overview (QC)

Shows, for each view, which patients have data. Gaps are patients missing that
assay; MOFA still uses their other views.

```{r overview, fig.width=8, fig.height=4}
for (cc in mofa_cancers) {
  f <- file.path(mofa_dir, paste0("mofa_", cc, "_corrected.hdf5"))
  if (!file.exists(f)) next
  print(plot_data_overview(suppressWarnings(load_model(f))) + ggplot2::ggtitle(cc))
}
```
